text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- Free Democrat President Ivan Peto said that the parliamentary group of his party wants Parliament to accept the conflict of interest bill rejected by President Arpad Goncz in order to pass it unchanged or in a more stringent form. @

- The final report filed by the supervisory committee of the State Privatisation and Holding Co. (APV) summing up the results of an investigation into the Tocsik affair says those responsible include the privatisation minister, the top executives of the APV, its board of directors and senior legal counsel. The report states that lawyer Marta Tocsik did not do any work at her own initiative for the company.
- French President Jacques Chirac said on Tuesday ahead of his official visit to Budapest on Thursday that Hungary will have a place in the European Union by 2000. @

- Visiting Ukrainian Foreign Minister Hennady Udovenko said his country respects Hungary's right to join NATO, but Kiev insists that Ukraine's national security consideration be taken into account as the military alliance expands.

- The executive vice president of the Socialist Party Tuesday dismissed as a fabrication and a culled text a document carried by the daily Uj Magyarorszag purporting to set out the party's media strategy leading up to the next parliamentary elections.
- A total of HUF 88 billion from the central budget will be allocated for agricultural subsidies this year. @
- A contract was signed yesterday for a EU grant of ECU 4.3 million to the Hungarian Customs andf Excise Office.
- Investors have 80 days to submit their bids to win the concession rights of two national commercial TV channels.
NEPSZABADSAG
- Democratic Forum President Sandor Lezsak and Young Democrat leader Viktor Orban announced that they intend to field joint candidates at the 1998 parliamentary elections.
MAGYAR NEMZET @
- A parliamentary investigative committee's report on the oilgate affair attaches blame to the Finance Ministry for leaking sensitive information and not initiating a tender process.
MAGYAR HIRLAP

- Foreign Ministry spokesman Gabor Szentivanyi said the re-opening of the Hungarian consulate general in Romania and that of the Romanian one in Hungary could take up to six months but the necessary funds are still missing. @

- Bomb experts and dozens of policemen equipped with automatic pistols swooped down on the immediate neighbourhood of the US Embassy in Budapest after an unidentified caller threatened to blow up the building yesterday. No explosives were found.
- MOL shares with a total face value of HUF 32 billion will be offered in two instalments to domestic and international investors in the first and fourth quarters of this year.
- The ceramics manufacturer Zalakeramia yesterday revealed details of its plannes share issue. @
- ABN Amro Bank will formally assume ownership of Magyar Hitel Bank on Monday.
NEPSZAVA

- Energy prices will be raised quarterly, as of January, the head of the Hungarian Energy Office said adding the price will be adjusted to import prices, the forint exchange rate, the inflation of production prices and environmental protection fees.
-- Budapest newsroom (36-1) 327 4040
